summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with T1-T2 paraplegia and a history of COPD and recurrent pneumonias, was admitted for shortness of breath, cough, and low-grade fever. Imaging showed bibasilar opacities consistent with atelectasis rather than new pneumonia. She was treated for a COPD exacerbation with a five-day course of prednisone, levofloxacin, and nebulized bronchodilators. Her symptoms improved during the two-day stay, though she remained on 2L oxygen at discharge. Chronic conditions including hypothyroidism, anxiety, and chronic pain were managed with continued home medications. A one-week supply of oxycodone and methadone was provided due to a missed pain management appointment. She was discharged home with service to follow up with her primary care provider.
